To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a water droplet oscillates in a uniform electric filed for electric field intensity less than a critical value, and that the droplet elongates until a jet is formed for electric field intensity above the critical value.
the droplet oscillates and elongates for weaker and stronger electric fields, respectively.
the droplet oscillates in a uniform electric filed for weaker electric fields, and elongates and breaks up into a jet when the electric field is strong enough.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of a water droplet in an electric field and the resulting jet formation.
the dynamics of a liquid droplet under a uniform electric field.
the study of the dynamics of water droplets in uniform and nonuniform electric fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the numerical predictions of the droplet deformation and break-up are in reasonable agreement with the available experimental results.
the distortion of a water droplet is governed by a balance between two forces, i.e. electric field induced forces and surface tension forces.
the droplet oscillates and elongates until it breaks up for sufficiently strong electric field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a numerical method to study the deformation and break-up of water droplets in a uniform electric fields and we have used the method to study the dynamics of the deformation and break up of a water droplet for different electric field strengths and droplet sizes.
the droplet oscillates in the weak electric field region and elongates in the strong electric field region.
the droplet distortion is governed by the electric field and the surface tension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the droplet distortion and the jet formation are governed by the same mechanism.

the electric field intensity required for the droplet elongation and jet formation can be significantly reduced when the droplet is placed in a dielectric liquid, as compared with the case of a free droplets.
the droplet distortion and break-up in a uniform electric filed can be described by a single dimensionless number, which is the ratio of the electric field strength to the critical field strength.
